title: Validate and change the Annals corpus
summary: Submit strict evidence-grounded reconciliations, inspect and apply current proposals, and read, normalize, or revert append-only corpus history.
use_when: A proposed corpus transition must be submitted, inspected, validated, or explicitly applied.
A reader needs commit, diff, normalization, or reversion guarantees.
do_not_use_when: An AI examination, source retention, or scheduled inbox operation is wanted.
The proposed change bypasses evidence, graph invariants, currentness, or supported history interfaces.
outcome: A complete validated interpretation, atomic authorized corpus transition, or exact read of append-only history.
effects: Submission records normalized reconciliation intent and provenance without changing corpus state.
Application atomically appends one commit and its canonical effects; mechanically equal results are recorded without a commit.
Confirmed nonempty shake removes only transitively implied direct edges; revert appends the inverse of one earlier transition.
Inspection, validation, log, and diff are read-only.
authority: Annals owns strict reconciliation input, structural validation, currentness, canonical effects, application, and append-only corpus history.
Stored library instructions define semantic interpretation; structural validity does not assert conceptual truth.
success: The selected request resolves and validates against its original base.
An authorized change commits atomically at its current corpus and instruction basis, or an exact read or no-change result is returned.
failure_and_recovery: Stale corpus or instruction state fails without force or silent rebase.
A normalization plan fails atomically if its identity, HEAD, graph, or instruction basis is stale.
Relevant intervening changes cause an atomic revert_conflict; unrelated facts survive.
History replay failure invalidates the library; direct SQL edits and skipped effects are unsupported recovery.
privacy: Library state retain complete source material, exact evidence, instruction revisions, reconciliation provenance, and corpus history. Keep them private.

interfaces.label: Submit a strict reconciliation
interfaces.invocation: annals change submit INPUT --work LABEL --base REVISION

interfaces.label: Inspect or validate a proposal
interfaces.invocation: annals change show --work LABEL; annals change validate --work LABEL

interfaces.label: Read corpus history
interfaces.invocation: annals log [--limit N]; annals diff FROM TO

does_not_authorize: Applying, normalizing, or reverting without authority for material effects.
Direct SQL, source rewriting, force application, history deletion, or disclosure.

consumers.statement: Local users, agents, and callers of the provider-owned reconciliation types may submit, inspect, validate, or explicitly apply one corpus transition and inspect or change history.

preconditions.statement: The selected prepared Annals library contains the scoped retained work and base revision. Application requires unchanged HEAD and selected instruction revision. Material effects require explicit authority.

inputs.statement: Strict JSON has a nonempty summary, one or more operations, and optional inert nonempty annotations. Unknown fields are rejected. The host selects work and base outside that semantic request.
Concept selectors use public cN IDs or same-request local creation handles. Evidence uses exact quotation plus optional heading and immediately adjacent-text filters, never source byte offsets.
The seven actions create, add/remove parent, add/remove evidence, reword with explicit evidence disposition, or nonrecursively retire with optional replacement.
Concept labels and handles cannot contain outer whitespace or control characters; labels may repeat and never select identities.
No move, sibling position, primary parent, arbitrary graph write, force application, or history deletion is supported.

outputs.statement: Full reconciliation reads distinguish resolved_operations from material effects and give evidence occurrence_count without byte ranges, actor/time, original request and relevant instruction provenance. Applied and recorded receipts are compact; pending proposals retain complete review content. change list defaults to 20 and uses schema-two items/has_more.

data_semantics.statement: A reconciliation is a provisional interpretation, not a unique semantic decomposition. It projects complete state at its original base. Every final leaf has evidence and the parent graph remains acyclic with valid endpoints.
Annotations are retained context and do not affect projection, equality, validation, or application. A selector matches all remaining quotation occurrences subject to bounded fan-out.
Annals stores normalized intent and append-only typed effects, derives current and historical state by the same strict reducer, and has no current-graph snapshot or stored resolved JSON authority.

identity_and_units.statement: Public cN identities survive rewording and are never reused, including IDs reserved during pending or superseded requests. Revision zero is empty; each accepted material transition advances exactly one contiguous integer revision.
Local handles and draft operation IDs are not concept identities. Work, reconciliation, and commit identity remain distinct.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Validation resolves the whole projected state at the original base. Application rechecks HEAD and instructions inside its committing transaction. Historical reads replay the requested immutable state.
No response-latency, corpus-size, or throughput objective is promised.

access.statement: Registered names and operator config/path selection use the libraries contract. Inspection and validation need read access to prepared state; mutations use the supported CLI and its typed client.
Direct SQLite edits and internal storage-row or source-offset integration are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: At most one reconciliation per work is pending. Same-or-later-base submissions supersede the prior pending record; older-base submissions do not displace newer pending results.

Mechanical equality is recorded without a commit. Material apply atomically appends canonical effects, marks the reconciliation applied, and completes linked delivery state when applicable; failures leave corpus and workflow state unchanged.

shake confirms an exact identity, HEAD, graph, and instruction basis. It preserves reachability but can change direct-neighbor counts, shared flags, paths, and hop distances. A later JSON preview does not bind a new invocation.
Revert appends an inverse to current HEAD without erasing history. Relevant incompatible intervening facts conflict atomically; unrelated facts survive.

Recorded and committed domain results survive later instruction changes and later execution failure. Legacy null instruction provenance remains unknown and cannot supply a current pending interpretation.

operational_limits.statement: Evidence links cover at most 8 KiB. Selection pages are bounded, while replay and in-memory state cost grow with history and corpus size. Normalization and reversion each create at most one new commit per successful material operation.
No general corpus capacity, completion latency, throughput, or cross-release historical support window is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Feature contract, release, library schema, reconciliation grammar, output schema, and Nucleus protocol evolve separately. Supported migration does not invent legacy instruction provenance.
No general pending-reconciliation or history deprecation window is promised.

reliances.statement: Annals libraries own selection, identity, kind, prepared-state access, and instructions. Corpus reading owns graph/evidence meaning and revision-bound read semantics.
These deterministic operations do not invoke a model, Nucleus, or a network service.
